fields.description: Largest file size (in megabytes) that opens as an in-browser preview.
fields.label: Preview Size

fields.description: Default storage quota per user (in megabytes). 0 means unlimited.
fields.label: Quota

fields.description: Default quota for Personal Drive roots, in bytes. 0 means unlimited.
fields.label: Default Personal Quota

fields.description: Default quota for the Shared Drive root, in bytes. 0 means unlimited.
fields.label: Shared Quota

fields.description: Where and how Drive lays out file contents — on the site's disk, or in the S3 bucket below.
fields.label: Storage Layout

fields.description: Prefix under private/files (or inside the bucket) where Drive keeps its content. Leave empty to store at the top level.
fields.label: Drive Folder

fields.description: Directory beside the file tree where generated thumbnails are kept.
fields.label: Thumbnail Prefix

fields.description:
Store files by id under one prefix instead of mirroring the folder tree.
S3 has no rename, so mirroring makes moving a folder copy and delete every object beneath it. Flat keeps moves and renames database-only.
Recommended for S3; leave off for local disk.
fields.label: Flat Storage

fields.description: Keep file contents in an S3-compatible bucket instead of on the site's disk.
fields.label: S3

fields.description: Store file contents in the bucket configured below instead of on the site's disk. Turning this on forces flat storage.
fields.label: Use S3

fields.description: Bucket that holds Drive's file contents.
fields.label: S3 Bucket

fields.description: Access key ID of an identity with read/write access to the bucket.
fields.label: AWS Key

fields.description: Secret access key for the identity above. Stored encrypted.
fields.label: AWS Secret

fields.description: S3 endpoint; S3-compatible providers (e.g. MinIO) work too. Example: https://s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com
fields.label: Endpoint URL

fields.description: Defaults to "s3v4". Some providers only support "s3".
fields.label: Signature Version

fields.description: Serve Drive over WebDAV at /dav so file managers and sync tools can connect. Each user must also allow access in their own Drive settings.
fields.label: WebDAV

fields.description: Let WebDAV clients (Windows Explorer, Finder, rclone…) connect to Drive at /dav using Frappe login credentials.
fields.label: Enable WebDAV

fields.description: Comma-separated HTTP methods WebDAV clients may use; leave empty to allow all. Valid: OPTIONS, GET, HEAD, PUT, DELETE, PROPFIND, PROPPATCH, MKCOL, COPY, MOVE, LOCK, UNLOCK. OPTIONS is always allowed and GET implies HEAD. Example for read-only access: PROPFIND, GET.
fields.label: Allowed WebDAV Methods
